$\therefore$PF$\perp$AD,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$AGP=$90^\circ$,\\

First read the diagram as a rhombus ABCD with diagonal AC drawn, P lying on AC, E on side AB, and F on side BC; the text states PE is perpendicular to AB and PF is perpendicular to BC. From the text, the perimeter is 48, so each side of the rhombus is 12, and the total area is 48. Since diagonal AC divides the rhombus into two congruent triangles, area(ABC)=24. Because P lies on AC, triangle ABC is partitioned into triangles ABP and PBC. Their altitudes to bases AB and BC are PE and PF respectively, so 24 = (1/2)(AB)(PE) + (1/2)(BC)(PF) = (1/2)(12)(PE+PF). method.method_draft: Use the extension-and-congruence route. First read the diagram as a rhombus ABCD with AD parallel BC, AB parallel CD, P on diagonal AC, PE meeting AB at E, and PF meeting BC at F. Extend the line FP upward until it meets AD at a point G. Since PF ⟂ BC and AD ∥ BC, PG is also perpendicular to AD. In a rhombus, diagonal AC bisects angle DAB, so ∠EAP = ∠GAP. Triangles AEP and AGP are right triangles sharing AP and having the same acute angle at A, so they are congruent; hence PE = PG. Therefore PE+PF = PG+PF = GF. Now use the text data: side BC = 48/4 = 12, and the rhombus area is base BC times height GF, so 48 = 12·GF. Thus GF = 4, giving PE+PF=4.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in rhombus $ABCD$, point $P$ is a moving point on the diagonal $AC$. Through point $P$, draw $PE \perp AB$ at point $E$, and $PF \perp BC$ at point $F$. If the perimeter of rhombus $ABCD$ is 48 and its area is 48, what is the value of $PE+PF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $FP$ to meet $AD$ at point $G$, as shown in the figure:\\
In rhombus $ABCD$, $AD\parallel BC$, $\angle DAC=\angle BAC$,\\
Also, $\because PF\perp BC$,\\
$\therefore PF\perp AD$,\\
$\therefore \angle AGP=90^\circ$,\\
$\because PE\perp AB$,\\
$\therefore \angle AEP=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AEP=\angle AGP$,\\
Also, $\because \angle EAP=\angle GAP$, $AP=AP$,\\
$\therefore \triangle EAP\cong \triangle GAP$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore GP=EP$,\\
$\because$ the perimeter of rhombus $ABCD$ is 48,\\
$\therefore BC=12$,\\
$\because$ the area of rhombus $ABCD$ is 48, i.e., $BC\cdot FG=48$,\\
$\therefore FG=48\div 12=4$,\\
$\therefore PE+PF=GF=\boxed{4}$.

Reasoning: The perimeter of rhombus ABCD is 48, so each side length is 48 ÷ 4 = 12, that is, AB = BC = 12. Diagonal AC of the rhombus divides the rhombus into two congruent triangles, so the area of triangle ABC is half of the area of the rhombus: 48 ÷ 2 = 24.
